questions.text: With INJECT_FAULT=1, at which fixed word address should the wrong value appear each pass, and is it a single corrupted read at that address, or something else (for example a stuck bit)? REQ-18 needs MARCH_FIRST_ERR to equal this address.
questions.answer: The fault appears at word address 5. It is one wrong word per pass, injected only in the checker's compare and never in the stored data, so it is not a stuck bit in the RAM. On the first pass it sets MARCH_FIRST_ERR to 5.
questions.evidence: - INJECT_FAULT makes the test see one wrong word per pass at address 5; that error counts in MARCH_ERRS and, on the first pass, sets MARCH_FIRST_ERR to 5. The fault is injected only in the checker's compare, never in the stored data, so the RAM ends all zero as March C- leaves it.

questions.text: Does one pass run March C- twice (background 0 and then 1, and in which order), or does each pass use one background and the passes alternate? Which background does the last pass finish on? REQ-20 needs the RAM to read all zeros afterwards.
questions.answer: One pass runs March C- twice: first with the all-zero background, then with the all-one background. The passes do not alternate backgrounds. The spec does not say which background the last pass finishes on. It only says the RAM ends all zero as March C- leaves it, and the fault is injected only in the checker's compare, never in the stored data.
questions.evidence: March C- is: up(w0); up(r0,w1); up(r1,w0); down(r0,w1); down(r1,w0); down(r0), with the all-zero background and then the all-one background as the data.  One pass is both backgrounds.

questions.text: What value does h_rdata show for the read of SCRATCH issued during reset hold? (Scenario: SCRATCH was written 0xDEADBEEF. The power-on counter reset is not re-asserted, but configuration just completed and rst is held for 8 clocks. A read of 0x008 is issued at clock 3 of the reset hold.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?

After rst deasserts, what is BUSY? (Scenario: A March run is in progress (BUSY=1, MARCH_ERRS=3) when rst is asserted for 8 clocks.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: BUSY is 0 after rst deasserts. The reset values list MARCH_STATUS as 0, so the interrupted run is abandoned: BUSY, DONE and passes completed are all 0. MARCH_ERRS also resets to 0.
questions.evidence: - Reset: MEM_ADDR 0, MEM_CTRL 0 (AUTOINC off), MARCH_CTRL 0, MARCH_PASSES 1, MARCH_STATUS 0, MARCH_ERRS 0, MARCH_FIRST_ERR 0xFFFFFFFF. The RAM contents are not reset by the bus reset; they hold 0xC0DE0000 + i from configuration.

questions.text: Which RAM word receives the value, and what is MEM_ADDR afterwards (give MEM_ADDR as int)? (Scenario: AUTOINC=1, MEM_ADDR=7. Host writes 0xAAAA5555 to RAM_DATA.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: RAM word 7 receives 0xAAAA5555 (stored at the old MEM_ADDR), and MEM_ADDR becomes 8.
questions.evidence: A RAM_DATA write with AUTOINC stores at the old MEM_ADDR and then increments; a RAM_DATA read does the same for reads.

questions.text: REQ-34 runs March C- with the all-zero background and then the all-one background in every pass. The last element, any(r d), leaves the RAM at d, so the all-one run ends with every word 0xFFFFFFFF, which contradicts REQ-20 (all zeros after the run). Should the RAM hold all zeros after a completed run, and if so, should the all-one background run first, or should a final clearing step be added? Or is the all-ones state the intended result?
questions.answer: Yes, the RAM must hold all zeros after a completed run; the specification states this twice. It does not say how to get there (running the all-one background first, adding a clearing step, or anything else), so that part is not specified. All-ones is not the intended end state.
questions.evidence: Afterwards the RAM must hold all zeros, which is where March C- leaves it.

questions.text: What is the top module called and in which file, and what instance name should jtag_bus have inside it, so the register-port bench and the build can find them?
questions.topic: Names, files and the build target
questions.answer: The top-level module is `p2_bram_rom_top`, in `rtl/p2_bram_rom_top.sv`. The bench drives the separate core module `p2_bram_rom_core` (`rtl/p2_bram_rom_core.sv`), not the top. The specification does not give an instance name for jtag_bus, so that part is not specified.
questions.evidence: - Names and files: the top-level module is named `p2_bram_rom_top` in `rtl/p2_bram_rom_top.sv`; the register-port core (the logic behind the `h_*` port, with no vendor primitive) is a separate module named `p2_bram_rom_core` in `rtl/p2_bram_rom_core.sv`, with ports `clk`, `rst` (active high), `h_we`, `h_re`, `h_addr[11:0]`, `h_wdata[31:0]`, `h_rdata[31:0]` and the design's own signals. Files are SystemVerilog (`.sv`). The bench drives the core.

questions.text: Which word does the read return, and where does MEM_ADDR point afterward? Pick the behaviour. (Scenario: AUTOINC=1, MEM_ADDR=7, RAM[7]=0xC0DE0007. Software writes 0x12345678 to RAM_DATA, then immediately reads RAM_DATA.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: The write stores 0x12345678 at the old MEM_ADDR 7 and then MEM_ADDR becomes 8. The following RAM_DATA read returns the word at 8, which is 0xC0DE0008 if nothing has written it, not the value just written. That read then increments MEM_ADDR to 9.
questions.evidence: A RAM_DATA write with AUTOINC stores at the old MEM_ADDR and then increments; a RAM_DATA read does the same for reads.

questions.text: Is MARCH_ERRS exactly 3 at completion (yes) or can it be a different number (no)? (Scenario: INJECT_FAULT=1 and a run of 3 passes completes. Each pass runs March C- twice (zero and one backgrounds) and the checker sees one wrong word at address 5 in each pass.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Yes. With INJECT_FAULT set and 3 passes, MARCH_ERRS is exactly 3, because the test sees one wrong word per pass (a pass being both backgrounds) and each one counts.
questions.evidence: - INJECT_FAULT makes the test see one wrong word per pass at address 5; that error counts in MARCH_ERRS and, on the first pass, sets MARCH_FIRST_ERR to 5. The fault is injected only in the checker's compare, never in the stored data, so the RAM ends all zero as March C- leaves it.

questions.text: Does RAM_DATA read 0xC0DE0064 (the initial value) after the reset? (Scenario: A March run is interrupted by reset when RAM holds partially written March data (e.g. RAM[100]=0xFFFFFFFF). After reset deasserts, software sets MEM_ADDR=100 and reads RAM_DATA.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: No. The reset does not restore the initial value. The RAM contents are not reset by the bus reset, so RAM[100] keeps whatever it held (0xFFFFFFFF in this scenario) and RAM_DATA reads that value. The 0xC0DE0000 + i values apply only from configuration, not after a reset.
questions.evidence: - Reset: MEM_ADDR 0, MEM_CTRL 0 (AUTOINC off), MARCH_CTRL 0, MARCH_PASSES 1, MARCH_STATUS 0, MARCH_ERRS 0, MARCH_FIRST_ERR 0xFFFFFFFF. The RAM contents are not reset by the bus reset; they hold 0xC0DE0000 + i from configuration.

questions.text: What happens to the run? (Scenario: START is written while BUSY=1 from a run in progress (3 of 10 passes done).) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: START while BUSY is ignored, so the run in progress continues unaffected: the counters, errors and passes completed are not cleared and the test carries on to the end.

questions.answer: MEM_ADDR reads 0, because with AUTOINC a ROM_DATA read adds 1 to MEM_ADDR and it wraps from 1023 to 0 (the read returns the ROM word at address 1023, and the increment happens after the data is captured).
questions.evidence: With AUTOINC, MEM_ADDR wraps from 1023 to 0.

After release, software reads ROM word 1023 and RAM word 1023 with no prior write.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: 0xC0DE03FF. RAM word 1023 holds 0xC0DE0000 + 1023 from configuration, and the reset does not change it. The 8-clock reset therefore has no effect on the value.
questions.evidence: The RAM contents are not reset by the bus reset; they hold 0xC0DE0000 + i from configuration.

A reset occurs (rst asserted then deasserted). No START is written afterwards.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: 0 (0x00000000). SCRATCH resets to 0, so after the reset it reads 0 and the earlier 0x12345678 is lost.
questions.evidence: | 0x008 | SCRATCH | RW | 32 bits, reads back what was written, resets to 0 |

questions.text: What value does the read return, and what is MEM_ADDR after that read? Give the value returned by the read. (Scenario: AUTOINC=1, MEM_ADDR=a=20, RAM[20]=0xC0DE0014. Software writes 0xAAAAAAAA to RAM_DATA. Then MEM_ADDR is set back to 20 and RAM_DATA is read.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: The read returns 0xAAAAAAAA, and MEM_ADDR is 21 afterwards. With AUTOINC, the write to RAM_DATA stores at the old MEM_ADDR (20) and then increments it to 21. MEM_ADDR is then set back to 20, so the RAM_DATA read returns RAM[20], which now holds 0xAAAAAAAA rather than 0xC0DE0014. The read uses the old address and then increments, so MEM_ADDR ends at 21.
questions.evidence: - A RAM_DATA write with AUTOINC stores at the old MEM_ADDR and then increments; a RAM_DATA read does the same for reads.

questions.text: What happens: does the run complete immediately with DONE=1, does it never terminate, or is it ignored? (Scenario: START is written with a passes value of 0 while BUSY=0.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Not ignored, and it does not finish at once or hang. With MARCH_PASSES at 0, START runs the test with the pass count max(1, 0) = 1, so it runs exactly one pass. BUSY is high for that pass, then DONE rises and BUSY falls in the same clock. The MARCH_PASSES register still reads back 0.
questions.evidence: MARCH_PASSES of 0 is treated as 1; the register keeps the value written (the pass count used is max(1, value)).
